I saw this maybe two months ago on the steam page, and the impression it left kept me checking every couple weeks until it released, and here it is!
I'm a huge fan of other RTS games such as Starcraft, Command & Conquer, Stronghold, and many more. Personally I think that if you were to compare this to a popular RTS, it would more closely match up with the Stronghold franchise the most. It has resource, space, building, and citizen management, with no actual control over the workers. You do however have a direct control over your military units and have the ability to pause the game to build your city the best way possible.
While I'm initially inclined to say that there isn't much content here, this is still early access at the time of this review. There is already a solid strategy and management core gameplay loop, with mechanics that work fluidly, and feel fun! There is a learning curve that provides a hefty challenge even at low difficulty levels, but once you start to understand and flesh out your game winning strats, the difficulty mostly comes in to the map layouts and challenges.
So far, I'm entranced with this game, and I can't wait to see the content that gets added to it. I'd love to see a few more survival tilesets, further difficulty customization, and of course I can't wait for the story campaign features.
Overall, it's a very fun and interesting colony builder/management/survival game, and if that's your jam, then give it a try!

So, for now, I have to put this as a positive review because I've dumped ♥♥♥♥ing hours since it came online. It's fun, BRUTAL, and I like the feel. However, as it's early access, I do have qualms to help the devs better their game.
Biggest issues I have so far:
- Right off the bat you'll notice no music. It feels eerie when you're hearing all the dogs, crows and random groans with nothing to supplement it. I go with some nam music and get the 'commie burning' goin'.
- Lack of tutorial meant I was trying my hardest to scum through the beginning of the game without help. It wasn't until this review that I managed to make it to the last hours on the 'default' settings of challenging... and yet still lost with 4 of the chaingun towers on each of my fronts, along with Titans and Lucifers.
- The whole 'No forgiveness' clause; with the inability to save minus LEAVING the game, you're boned. Set up defenses on the north to defend most of the waves? Sorry charlie, they decide to hit your weakest point down south. Let that one roamer past when you didn't see him? Whoops, there goes your entire population.
I get it, it's meant to be hard, but for the first few days of playing it felt near impossible.
- Random level seeds. Sure, it can help, but it can also cuck. The times I got some pretty damn good defense seeds they end because a zombie makes it through a one tile space I didn't know existed and was suddenly infecting my population centers. Other times you can be left with absolutely nothing to start off and vast spaces to try and cover in defenses. It's a tad rediculous - resource wise - to cover ANYTHING but a choke point.
- The whole 'you need to win a 75% match to get a new tile set. I'm sorry, 100 days on default with no time dilation increase makes a 100 day game take hours to do. 80 days on low population hordes is about the same as more days with bigger hordes. You.. really can't chose one or the other, and there's no point in messing with the settings at first until you can SOMEHOW make it past the first level with a decent seed.
Now if this was based on score, and not 'completionist' I would absolutely love it to death. My record is 1240 on a 75% run with a pretty bad starting area on the seed..
- Lack of units. Ya, I had to put this. You have more building types then you do units, and you only get your third type if you can manage to get the wood shop. ( Which, in my honest opinion, the sniper is the BEST unit. A vet sniper can one shot any zed minus spitters, harpy's and fat ♥♥♥♥s. Leave those to the ballista towers. Zeds around them explode when it hits)
- Unit AI seems lacking, and the way they target makes it a little rough if they're in a group. Sure, I can have 4 marines with two on level and two on closest, but sometimes that means they all still focus about the same target when they're getting swarmed. Couple this with the whole 'Whoops, I pathed into a tree, lemme just keep pushing into it for something to happen'...
- The inability to select combat units on the fly minus control groups. I'm ok with assigning control groups once my army gets a tad large and starts to include more than one squad, but if I have to drag my camera around my housing district to find that one sniper who's pathing is stuck on a house - one more time - I'll just have him executed if he DOES arrive to his destination.
- Speaking of housing. The 'colonist population' has nothing to do with the game until election points, which only happens at population intervals - and nine times out of ten the two choices give you absolute jack. I'd rather have a way to force the 'population' all into workers.. Something akin to 'Stalin or Gulag'.
But now that the bad is done, lets move on to the good:
- It reminds me of Starcraft and the days where there were some decent zombie survival customs online. If this had multiplayer, I would die and go to heaven.
- The whole steampunk asthetic is neat. Very few games do it well, and you guys get to take the award on this one away. It's refreshing, to say the least.
- Although it's unforgiving, like most reviews and jokers put it, it kinda draws you back in. Ya, you lost that last round because of this, how about trying this or this? Maybe it'll get you further - or maybe it was all because of your seed. Wanna risk it to find out? You're only gonna lose a few hours of your life... < _ <;
- It.. KINDA forces you to adapt? The only real thing you need to focus on is making sure your defenses are evenly spaced. They might've attacked you on the north the last 5 times, but the next might be from the south. Examine your lanes, try to do some zombie forcing, and get stone as fast as you can early on.
It's a short list of good, and a long list of complaints. Right now it feels like a rougelike that - like FTL - I'll hope to god I get lucky enough to win; but that's something I'd rather not do. Right now it feels like Mission Impossible, though if that's your thing go right ahead and torture yourself.
Good game though, even with the qualms.

This point and click adventure game by Alasdair Beckett-King and Application Systems Heidelberg feature a female pirate captain Nelly Cootalot. While working aboard a ship HMS Undeliverable that was delivering mail to Port Rubicund, Nelly receives a visit by her spiritual mentor Captain William Bloodbeard, telling her to pursue William's brother Baron Widebeard to stop him from a plot to hypnotize, control and raise an army of birds to go after an object of great power.
The game has more than 90 positive reviews at the time of this review, has a funny and entertaining cast of characters with funny and witty dialogue, great voiced dialogue and songs with vocals, cute and comical hand-drawn graphics and animation for every character and talking bird in the game, a fast travel option in one large port town and the option to show all objects and characters that Nelly can look and interact with and puzzles, minigames and achievements that are easy to solve, complete and obtain. Overall, highly recommended when at discount for those who like a great comedic point and click adventure game that is casual and forgiving for all types of players and don't mind a few minor bugs in the game. (I spotted 2 bugs during my playthrough, there is a bug that occurs rarely where sometimes selecting an item to try to combine with another item on inventory as an invalid item pair combination will somehow fail to close the inventory window and it is not possible to use the item on anything in the external environment until a delay afterwards. The second bug is the achievement Timewaster where it is not automatically awarded upon obtaining the second last achievement and the player has to close and restart the game to obtain the final achievement. Thank you ASHGAMES, Saraphel and Alexander Henn for working to fix this bug as mentioned in the game's discussion forums. Developers also appear to be quite responsive to bug reports on the game and have provided a contact e-mail in the game's discussion forums to address all reported bugs.)

As a seasoned veteran of this series having played the first game extensively both on PC and console I have to say its sequel is taking it to another level. HOWEVER! being an early access there are some things that could use a tweak. These little hiccups are what influence why I do but don't recommend this game.
It feels like it could be a game right now if the devs got lazy and published it now. Wouldn't be a good game but it would be a game.
To begin here are some cons to take into account.
-The only person voiced is Kovac (being in early access its no issue right now but if it hits beta and no voices then yeah, issue.)
-In combat there is no room for one mistake. Normally running around with a giant hammer would be slow however it is quite unforgiving if you swing half a second early. There have been multiple times my hammer grazed a zombie for no damage only because of how perfect they expect of you to time your shots. With guns theres no issue however seeing as i spray and pray with my machine gun. :)
-Crafting got lame
Pretty much to craft anything you need a specific building in your camp first, and you dont guess anymore (i loved the guessing game in the first one) the blueprints are right there for you to go GRIND for the parts which isn't how I remember the game. Not to mention there is only one model/type/look whatever for each weapon. The only thing that changes if you build another weapon is the stats. my level 30 rifle looks just like the one I had at lvl 5.
-Damage what are you doing?
Once again i'll be swingin my hammer and getting eaten but when I do land a blow it does a solid 1500k damage. Now after one hit killing about 5 zombies I go in for another kill and bam. 600 damage? What?
I figured this had to do with stamina and exhaustion and what not; which it does to an extent. Except i tested this. At full stamina i did 1,500 damage,and then 600 and then 900. huh? damage. go home. your drunk.
-Don't fight 2v1
You heard me. If you take on more than one zombie with a melee weapon. Your gonna get hurt, 100% of the time. In the first game if you did a power swing/charge thing whatever you hit all the zombies in front of you then you can dodge the one behind you. Well not anymore, if you swing not only is it slow but it also cripples your legs for whatever reason because you gotta wait a second to move again.
-Repetitive missions and lack of story
Each mission your either in a town or a swamp either fetching, killing, or finding some dude named Fan. the fetching and killing is okay (being devoted to the borderlands series im used to it) but I mean I just saved a guy from getting eaten and then I find him in the swamp wanting chocolate? then suddenly I have to go back to town to save him again. I mean i get that the dude could have traveled? But it feels lazy and thrown together. (Once again, EARLY ACCESS I get that it just bugs me)
-Zombie dog? or pelican?
There are various zombie animals, and they all sound the same. The zombie dogs make the exact same grunting noise as the zombie pelicans. Not much else to state here
Good things to look forward to
-Build to live!
You get to build a camp and defend it from the zombie horde. The buildings can all be upgraded and provides different crafting opportunities. I was sad that i couldnt build a turret. :P
-Crafting
As I said its pretty lame, but it is nice that I see what I need, I DON'T like how they handed me the blueprint however. maybe give me the blueprint after I figured it out?

I have to change my review because after coming out of EA and after several updates, the game has been left in the state it was, without improvement on gameplay.
tl;dr section is to be found at the end.
HTS2 adds crafting, base building, a longer story, and aliens to HTS1. Sadly MP have become the core aspect of the game, leaving behind the story and transforming SP into a grindfeast.
Uncommon enemies have been balanced only for MP. They possess a strong attack, a huge amount of health, and are either positioned in places you cannot run from (tunnels), hidden underwater (alligators), or have so much health you'll have to fight for dozen of minutes of frustrating hit and run (wererabbits and bears). I don't mind the odd though enemy, but these ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s stun your character at each attack while doing heavy damage, and need to be hit 20 to 40 times to die, all the while you are forced to run in circles. No strategy, pure time consuming running here and there. How fun does it sound?
Aliens - final enemies - attack in droves, have a ranged stunning attack, and can absorb whatever you throw at them. Good for MP, absolute waste of time in SP. They are just though and stay there shooting from a distance. Two hits and you are toast.
Some missions are extremely hard, a spike in difficulty that has no link to the plot. For example, you'll have to bring six pigs - one of the most dangerous critter in the game - into a barn. These pigs kill you in a few hits but get stuck into the decoration, you try to unstick them by running around, and when you suddenly succeed you are dead - because they run as fast as you. I had so much fun during this mission.
Maps are repetitive. During development this was a major gripe: decors are the same throughout the game. You have cities OR marshes. They did add a church, a fallen plane (where you get stuck a lot), and a barn. That's it. Because you have to repeat so many times the same missions (see base building) landscape gets old very quickly.
Maps have still many glitches, you'll find incomplete stairs, get stuck into beds, be blocked by invisible obstacles. Being chased by an invulnerable turtle and being blocked by a transparent branch isn't so fun.
Base building becomes a chore after level 10.
You'll spend more than half your time - 20 hours out of 35 - only to gather resources
to find the materials needed to build your camp. Maybe in MP this is fun, maybe MP players don't mind repeating missions, but in SP this is mindnumbingly boring.
As if the infinite repetition of the same mission wasn't enough, inventory management is a drag. Like mission variety, it has been forgotten during development. You can either move EVERYTHING in your inventory, or ONE thing at a time. No LeftShift+LMB to move, this would be too simple, you have to physically click and move every item, because othewise your inventory will be emptied of all the items you need - potitons and food and ammo. After each mission you'll come back to empty your pockets - and boy be ready to repeat the same missions a few times - and after each mission you'll have to put back in place the items needed to survive.
Resource gathering is so long that they did add a reminder of where you found a certain item, but items are not sorted, so be prepared to browse throughout the hundreds of items you have in your inventory before identifying the one you need, then read where you can find it.
As you may expect, each mission yields a few items, while the next level of your camp needs several dozens of this very item.
Not only each building goes through 50 levels, but they have only three different looks. How fun is that? Spending hours grinding for materials to build the next identical thing.
BUG - If you want to move your trunk (containing the items gathered during hours and hours of repeating the same mission), first build the new one, then empty the old one, because dismantling a trunk makes you lose everything WITHOUT A ♥♥♥♥ING WARNING. Thanks devs.
Before assembling a more powerful version of your weapon / armour / potion, you need to find the appropriate resources and improve your buildings. Like a research tree, each building level opens up new possibilities, but the game offers almost no information about what will be made available.
You will never know how many levels you have to build, before your much needed better rifle is available. Meanwhile an improved camp provokes the appearence of stonger zombies.
Again no strategy to be used here, just go on mindlessly gathering resources and improving buildings.
This game was promising during EA, but developers ignored SP and kept adding missions built using the same props and the same layout, duplicating items and camp levels to artificially lengthen the game, all the while ignoring needed "quality of life" improvements like a proper inventory mangement system, and ultimately transforming the game into a grindfeast.
Single players be warned.

Ive only played this game for about 5 Hours, and i love it. It has its ups, and downs when it comes to gameplay, but for the most part it is good fun.
Pros:
-Graphics are amazing - The qality is that of a AAA game, and very beautiful. I love the evironment, even the different weather effects like rain, and dust storms are very beautiful, and well shown. The sky is very beautiful as well showing different interstallar bodies like planets, and ring systems.
-Gameplay is very easy - I find navigating the different interfaces very easy, and everything falls in place just as it should. I havent found a need to change any of the contol bindings due to the fact that everything is already well placed, and that everything is easily accessable.
-Balance - The system is very fair when it comes to what resources you need to craft items. Although the aquisition of resources is a bit tedious it actually makes you work for things instead of the player simply being handed them.
-Atmosphere - The Environment is constantly changing around you addind to the different moods. Gathering resources in the dark is quite a frightening task especially since dark in this game is REALLY DARK, no residual light like in others, ITS DARK. All of those environmental changes coupled with the different alien creatures, and there behavior really adds to the frightening, unknown planet mood.
-Optimization - Although i have a good GPU the game preforms very well, and doesnt seem to tax my hardware even with the graphics settings maxed out.
Cons:
-Lens getting Dirty Inside - Even when you are within a sealed, oxigenated environment, your characters lens gets dirty by the weather effects, and different environmental effects.
-Difficult Recovery - It is very difficult to recover from death unless you have a substantial stock pile of resrouces. Possibly add an easier method of aquiring weapons early in game that can actually do damage to the enemies you encounter, this would be especially helpful on the trek to recover your dead body.
-Resources Grinding - Findind resrouce to begin with is very difficult due to the fact that your only told what you need, and not even what it looks like, or the area youd find it in, and unless you remeber the different lattitude, and longitude positions of the resource spawns finding more becomes difficult. Possibly add an ingame resources book that players can craft from basic materials that tell them about the different resources, and areas they may find them.
-Very little guidance - I found myself needing to visit the wiki more then playing the game because after you craft the Forge theres no more missions to guide you even through the basics like, drinking, eating, using your inventory properly, and your skill webs which is all major parts of game play. Possibly add an ingame guide, or quest book, or even intigrate the wiki into the game in order to help guide the player through the basics, and even the more adavanced aspects of the game.

Evolve Stage 2, better titled "Revenge of the Hunters"
OMG, where to even start?
Stealth gamplay options for the monster have been totally removed:
-Match timer drastically shortened, defaults to hunter win
-Hunters gain "planetary scanner" that tells them where the monster is every 30 seconds
No longer possible for the monster to evade a fight:
-All hunters can throw the arena, no more killing the trapper to improve monster mobility
-Mobile arena automatically centers on the monster, and can hit the monster from across the map
Monster can no longer control the pace of fight with targeted kills:
-All hunters can almost instantly revive fallen hunters; everyone is now Lazarus
-dropship respawn timer now starts with mission start, if monster doesn't kill all hunters in under 5 minutes, hunters are guaranteed to get at least one free round
From the original release, this game was balanced heavily in favour of the hunters:
-Each hunter has multiple lives, in the worst-case scenario, the monster must make 12 kills to win.
-Hunters have ridiculous damage-absorption abilities, somehow able to survive, repeatedly, being crushed under fists the size and weight of a small truck, bolts of energy that explode like blocks of C4, and massive bone-blades that cut through other megafauna with ease.
-Hunter damage output is insane, relative to their size:  Even with the assault down, a hunter team can easily pour enough firepower out to finish even a stage-3 monster if it has less than 50% remaining health.
With the new updates, the monster is forced to fight the hunters sooner, unable to flee or evade when wounded, and incapable of controlling the pace of the fight by being selective with kills.  This game is completely unenjoyable for someone who wants to play a cunning, vicious predator.  I felt cheated out of my money when I bought the game at launch and it turned out to be such trash, was legitimately cheated when my "Includes all monsters" season pass failed to include all monsters, and now the final insult: everyone gets for free that which i paid a premium for.
The only reason to play as a monster anymore is for the "BLARGH! SMASH!" factor, and the only reason to play a hunter is to get an ego-stroking.  They wanted to remake the game to appeal to the masses, well, good job, I suppose it will be a right smash amongst beer-guzzling football fans.

Well I wish I could have given this game a thumbs up, but sadly I cannot.
I picked up this game because people  said it was a "free to play game done right", so, with intrest I downloaded this game, weary of the F2P setup that the game had.
To my amazement AT FIRST this game was amazing! with interchangable build setups, skill trees, and objective-based pvp this game seemed like a sure winner in my book... it seemed to recreate my feelings of pre-cata WoW...however when you get to the game developers, you find problems.
What problems you may ask? Well for one classes aren't balanced, mages lag behind in damage (which is suppose to be their main job) vs other classes and spells do not scale well with level at all.. forcing you to use higher level spells, just to keep up with damage, as skills I got earlier seem to lose all their damage and appeal.. which is ESPECIALLY frustarating considering that melees can come up and do HUGE damage output without using more than a few skills + their heavy armor... the worst offender is the beastmaster (a warrior with a pet) that both do HUGE damage and can sweep most pvp matches. Balance is almost nonexsistant. The worst of this is that the devleopers have utterly lost intrest in the game, launching patches that fix absolutley none of these problems, or when they do, barely any of them at all.
The other problem is the part you're probobly not surprised about and that's the "soul packages" which are basically build options that are locked, unless you buy one fo these packcage, which will unlock them. This wouldn't be a problem if they weren't horrendiously overpriced... with the basic one for mages being $25! 25! for ONE classes builds.
Now there is an in-game tradeable currancy which allows you to buy things out of the in game store, and can be bought for cash, but good luck getting the money for one considering that you can't use the AH (untill you buy a package), and the fact that no one buys anything below end-game level anyways.
This game has "SWOTR" written all over it...it could've been a great game, but greedy/lazy developers soiled it with lazy, poor updates and horrible content.
I feel sorry for those whom bought this game when it was a monthly susbscription game... I really do, because you folks got screwed over...
The PVE in the game is fun, with little rifts all over the world with enemies that requrie you to team up with others to take down... other than that it's all the same here...dungeons, quests, you know the lot if you played other MMORPGS.
If you think that doing the same PVE content over and over again, just to get money to buy store-currancey is fun, than this game is worth a buy for you... but for me I expect a bit more out of a game that charges such outrageous prices for so little content.... 4/10. There's nothing really to see here.

Buy it on a sale. It's seriously not a bad game, for what it is.

As a fan of Double Fine's earlier efforts, especially Psychonauts, it's no surprise Costume Quest drew my attention with little effort. Given I'm also a fan of costuming and Halloween, this was pretty much an instant sell. Having fully completed the game, I can assure you it did not disappoint.
Right from the get-go, Costume Quest shows efforts to include every possible player, as you can choose to play as either the boy (Reynold) or girl (Wren) of a pair of twins. Soon after the twin you didn't select is kidnapped by monsters for dressing like a delicious-looking candy corn, you meet up with other trick-or-treaters your age that match your level of imagination and your desire to get your sibling back.
Costume Quest feels like an RPG stripped down to its essentials, with timing-centric, turn-based combat and set amounts of spawns in most areas. This, along with the enemies' leveling along with you, eliminates the need for experience grinding. Wiping out everything is still necessary for 100% completion and makes getting costume upgrades and some secrets easier, but you can get by if you stick to story-necessary encounters.
The game itself feels a bit small, area-wise, but there are plenty of tasks in each section to keep your party busy and searching for hidden items and secret costumes. A great balance is struck between backtracking through each section and forward progression, so it rarely, if ever, feels like a slog.
The variety of costumes is also nice, especially their in-combat forms. Due to the children's imaginations, whatever costume they're wearing transforms into a majestic, towering version of its mundane representation, all featuring beautiful animations and unique, often hilarious special attacks. As touched on before, combat is straightforward, with timed button presses coming into play on top of the base mechanics to lessen incoming damage and stack combos with your own attacks.
All in all, Costume Quest is relatively short, super sweet, and great for any time of year. Just remember that a couple of achievements (for the game and for the Grubbins On Ice DLC) are time-associated, so be ready to fire the game back up when more seasonably appropriate. You could just wiggle your PC clock a bit, but that'd be lame.

You control a group of trick-or-treaters that gain strength and powers based on the costumes they wear to battle evil candy stealing monsters from another dimension. You roam around the world, looking for candy, collectable cards, pieces of your costumes, and others things on a quest to save your brother or sister (the game changes based on if you play as a boy or girl).
The combat is a turn based affair with your kids gaining a special ability every 3rd turn, that based on their costume will either deal massive damage or heal or protect other teammates. It is very easy to master, and you get even more power-ups with the various stamps you collect. Towards the end game I felt the combat got slightly repetive and boring, maybe too easy for older gamers.
Even though the game is rather short, I can't really call it a negative in this case. If it went on to a 20+ hour game they would have to make a whole lot more additions to every aspect of the game. This tight little bundle of gaming is the perfect length and pacing for its content. Costume Quest is a fun and funny game to play.

Also - do not expect to win or that it will be simple or easy, even on "easy". For me that's an interesting challenge, but it can get frustrating - again, as an early access game with only an ironman survival mode at present, it can be dispiriting to watch as yet another colony you sunk time into is eaten by the infected.

As much as I enjoy this game, there is nothing that can stop me from recognising how utterly♥♥♥♥♥♥it is. At every available opportunity, the developers will attempt to screw you over for a little extra money to fill their pockets.
You can expect from this game:
--- A stunning, and aggressive lack of content. With the exception of a couple of favourites, nearly every country is lacking flavour text to make it at all interesting or different in experience.
--- Unrealistic gameplay. Due to balancing, an awful tech tree, and typically overpowered and samey national focus trees, the game does not play like a historical simulation to any concievable degree, despite what it claims to be. As opposed to a grand strategy game, it feels more like a "WWII themed sandbox."
--- Boring gameplay. For years of the game, there will be nothing to do except hit alt+tab and have fun while you wait for the game to become fun. If you're not at war, it is boring, and even when at war, it feels boring and tedious after you figure out the God-awful AI's favourite strategies and how to easily counter them. At the hardest difficulty, which actively boosts AI performance and degrades your own through modifiers on production, research, and army organisation, the AI still makes decisions that rookie players could find fault with.
--- Simple mechanics. There is not in-depth and hardcore design to the game found in other, older Paradox titles such as Victoria II, or even the constantly updated EUIV. These games require experience to play, and have a learning curve that allows the player to start every new game with more and more skill. HOI4 does not. It is simple, easy to figure out and does not change.
--- An active modding community. One of the only good things about this game is its modding community, which has made many features and developments that make the game, which has been developed by a studio specifically catred to grand strategy games, look in comparison bland and boring. Look at Kaiserreich for example, whose gameplay FAR outmatches the base game.
--- DLC whoring. Expect the game to feel absolutely garbage for years to come. While Stellaris has far superceded this game in terms of content and playability, HOI4 still drags its feet through the special kid's special sandbox. It's actually awfully unfun.

Nelly Cootalot is a point-and-click adventure game where you star as an amateur/ferocious (??) pirate named Nelly.
In short, this game is very much like a long lost "Monkey Island" sequel that was never released. Nelly could well be Guybrush's and Elaine's daughter, if they ever got one. She's got Elaine's red hair and attitude, and Guybrush's witty and quirky sense of humour. Like the latter, she wants to be a pirate, but is absolutely clueless about how life at sea works.
The humour is the best part of the game. It's witty and, once again, resembles Monkey Island in almost every aspect, though with a few twists. The graphics are gorgeous. Everything is hand-drawn and incredibly detailed. You can stare at the backgrounds for minutes, over and over, and still notice new things each time you come back. The characters are fun and memorable (highlights include a Dylan-wannabe busker and a great, spooky villain by the name of Van Zandt). The soundtrack is above average and fits very well with the game.
The puzzles are well-balanced. It's fun to figure out what you're supposed to be doing and they're never too difficult. It may take some time to realize what you're supposed to do sometimes, but most of the time, you just have to think a little bit and explore the wonderful backgrounds in the game and look for details you can use. In other words, it's even a joy to get stuck and come back later. You want to come back to the game.
Nelly's charmingly British accent is also welcome in an over-exaggerated market of mostly American games. It also adds to the witty nature of the game.
The only criticism I have is that the game is relatively short. I finished it in a total of seven hours in my first run. It would also be nice to have a higher difficulty setting to choose, so you could come back later and explore even more things. There are also some problems with the control, where you sometimes have to wait for Nelly walk to the next room once you've clicked, even if you click on something else before she gets there. But these complaints are very minor.
Overall, I absolutely loved this game. It takes me back to a time (circa 1997) when point-and-click adventures were still around and flourishing. It's the best find I've done in quite a while and the perfect compliment for you if you're waiting the Monkey Island sequel that never arrives.

Nelly Cootalot: The Fowl Fleet is the sequel to a free game that was released quite some time ago. I didn't realize that while playing the game until I Googled. There are several moments in the game that allude to the previous game in some way, such as the opening.  That said you really don’t need to play the previous game to enjoy this one, only know that a world and characters already exist.
The game channels much of Secret of Monkey Island unabashedly. It’s even brought up in game.  That’s okay. Nelly Cootalot takes similar world and works with its own themes. There’s not a lot swashbuckling, mostly fetching drinks and food for people, also insurance fraud. The game goes for the same zany if it puns it works logic that Monkey Island did, but it doesn’t go nearly as far as they did. (Anyone remember the Monkey Wrench?)
Puzzle are pretty simple, a no point did I feel the need to search for hints. Many puzzles are pun related, some are just fetch quests, nothing that requires deep thought.  If anything, the simplicity of the puzzles is the weakest point of the game, but not so bad as to not recommend it.
The voice acting is solid, with Tom Baker standing out far ahead of the rest. While he is does have a major roll, it’s in the form of a hint/helper.  Aside from a handful of puzzles, you really don’t need to speak to his character often. Hints just aren’t that necessary. I found myself interacting with the character just cause.
There was 1 minor bug, hotspots would stop working randomly. Not a huge issue, but could make completing achievements trickier.
Overall, a great game, simple but with a lot of love and care put into it.

Nelly Cootalot: The Fowl Fleet is a delightful adventure game with fantastic humor, a surprisingly large cast of characters (with great voice acting), and puzzles which are, indeed, quite fair.  What difficulty there is generally just comes from the game's "main" middle area which is the largest, and simply has an awful lot to explore and look through before you can get a good handle on what your goals are.  If you ever do feel at a loss for what to do, the game thoughtfully allows you to ask your sidekick Sebastian, who will provide some pointers.  It's a great touch.  The game follows the Lucasarts philosophy of adventure games, so it's impossible to get into a no-win situation.
The main draw really is the humor, and the excellent delivery with which the lines are generally given.  Tom Baker, as Sebastian, is of course great, but Nelly Cootalot herself is voiced flawlessly, and it was a treat to have her as the protagonist.  There were many times I laughed out loud (for real!), and many lines I couldn't resist sharing with friends.
Anyway: highly recommended if you enjoy this kind of adventure game.  I'm looking forward to any more Nelly Cootalot adventures which may find their way to release!

So I admit I'm pleasantly surprised with this one. Being Ubisoft I fully expected it to be awful, buggy, unplayable and riddled with microtransactions. Several of those hold true to this day, with at least one of them never even having a chance of being changed.
Most weapons (aside from a few promotional crossovers and things like the lever action rifle) are unlockable via exploration, all weapon attachments are unlockable in the same way. Free bonuses for owning certain other games (assassin's creed, rainbow six and a couple of others) that can be purchased should you choose to do so without getting said games. Lots of cosmetics locked behind a paywall, which is a minor annoyance at best.
While I have yet to play it, the season pass does not seem to be worth it. Though as far as I know it's the only way to unlock a select few of the 'bonuses' it comes with (which is supposed to justify costing $10 more than the only two DLC campaigns it includes if you were to buy them separately).
The singleplayer is okay at best, sync shots make no sense whatsoever, with your squadmates able to take shots at distances most players would struggle with... Through multiple hard covers and with no line of sight. The AI generally ignores your squadmates entirely and pretends they don't exist (and the few times they actually try to shoot someone they're almost useful because of this).
The co-op is where this game really shines. The non-existent physics, awkward and braindead helicopter controls, repetitive missions and generic story are completely shoved to the side in the pure fun that happens when you play this game co-op (I'd even say the laughably bad physics occasionally help add to it). There are multiple approaches to any given location, though most of them tend to end with various things exploding and an all-out attack from both sides.
tl;dr bring a friend or three for co-op if you plan to pick this one up. Pubbing it is alright at best, singleplayer is boring as hell. Oh and I guess there's a pvp mode or something.

I can say, first and foremost, that this is a visual novel. Regardless of sub-genre, that's what this boils down to.
It's a very intriguing visual novel. It performs under the guise of a classic Japanese high school dating sim while donning the peculiar gimmick of having birds for the school's students. While this may sound extremely gimmicky, and I won't lie, it is. That is not necessarily a bad thing though! This allows for a different kind of exploration into one's feelings.
You would not think so, but these birds are essentially people-type characters. They talk, have inner/outter conflicts, and even run in marathons. I can also imagine the same could happen if it was a high school of
, but it's not. That would be an awesome game. We need that to be on Steam right now.
If you're still interested at this point you'd might as well start reading further into this. Let's face it; if you're interested in a dating sim with birds, then you probably have few other things to entertain you at this point in terms of modern gaming.
That's how I felt, but I was tired of the typical tropes of AAA games and decided that I would instead let myself fall victim to the cliches of standardized Japanese gaming this time around. I was absolutely correct in the aspect of dating sim cliches remaining intact, but I was not prepared for the fact that there are routes that rip the afforementioned apart. If you're reading through Fate/Stay Night, then of course you'd expect things to become intense and heavy. When you play an average dating sim you're just expecting two people to get together and happy things ensue with a nice ending, save for School Days. That was just depressing on about every level.
You won't expect things once they hit you in Hatoful Boyfriend, and that is the true glory of the writing in this game. It just happens to be covered in a feathery layer topped with a beak.
I fully recommend this title to visual novel enthusiasts, or anyone who just wants to dive into the visual novel genre for their first time. With a title like this being easily accessible to a North American audience on Steam, there has never been a better time to start!

I feel this game has been unfairly maligned in official press reviews. Personally, I enjoyed it a great deal, even though I'm a fan of classic Xcom turn based gameplay, as I don't think the two are mutually exclusive! Yes, there are problems with the game, but there is also a lot of fun to be had along the way.
The positives: Evocative, interesting setting...early 1960's Americana, which unlike tropes like modern warfare or space marines, hasn't been done to death in video games.
Challenging, tactical third person shooter gameplay. A fair few options to pick from during combat. Different combinations of characters, like sniper, support guy, commando and engineer, allow you to tailor your squad to your own tastes for a variety of play styles.
Enjoyably hokum B movie storyline, with a few twists and turns.
Interesting variety of weaponry, particularly when you start to unlock the cool alien stuff!
The negatives: Your AI squadmates will need babysitting...a lot! Unless you're happy for them to fall in combat within the first two minutes of a firefight!
The mass effect style waypoint markers for your abilities and squad orders act like real physical objects when you are moving them around the scenery. This means that they are constantly getting stuck and you end up frustrated in your attempts to put them exactly where you want them. As an example, if you are trying to position an ability up on a ledge full of enemies, you can't just elevate the marker up into the air, you have to walk the marker to the nearest ramp and all the way around the environment until you get to the ledge and if that means that you go outside the ability's area of effect, then you are unable to position it...absolutely ludicrous! This was a glaringly, stupid mistake by the developers and led to much frustration on my part!
The base is a bit of a missed opportunity. It feels a bit lifeless. You just wander around and talk to people, with the odd mini side mission thrown in. I would have liked to have been more actively involved in the research and development of new equipment and weaponry, for instance, finding components out in the field and bringing them back to base, in order to upgrade weapons etc.
This game is crying out for a co-op mode, which would have mitigated the negative aspect of having such useless NPC AI and would have generally elevated the game to near classic status in my eyes. Discussing tactics with a friend or two and then executing our plans together would have been brilliant!
Story have a lot holes but the setting and the mood makes up for it. The shooting and tactical part of combat makes The Bureau a pretty fun experience, especially when you buy the game on sale.

If you haven't heard about this game, let me be the first to tell you that you aren't missing out. Do not buy it until it is on steam sale (which should be relatively soon at this rate). Here are a few reasons why I say this about The Bureau: XCOM Declassified:
1) The game is extremely buggy. I fell off the map into oblivion at least a dozen times for one reason or another. I even have a screenshot of it occurring and me simultaneously dying. Top this off with a few animation glitches, enemies not spawning or allowing you to progress, and you are setting yourself up for repeating some parts or entire battles in a mission.
2) It has an autosave feature only. No option like in XCOM: Enemies Unknown for what kind of save system you want. This is atrocious when mixed with all the bugs in the game aforementioned.
3) The game is disappointingly short. It took my crappy laptop longer to download the game than to actually play through it--and I completed every side/optional mission as well (My achievements are proof of that).
4) Your companions/troops are utterly useless to you. I have screenshots that show just how little they actually contribute to the mission. Hardly any kills, don't know how to use cover effectively, die too often, and literally run into grenades after avoiding them due to a slight time delay in their detonation. It is unbearably annoying, and doesn't improve as they level up.
5) After you get about halfway through the campaign, you just repeat the same tactics nonstop. This gets repetitive and detracts from the overall interest in the game. You defeat the enemies in the same methods over and over, and it doesn't leave you feeling like you accomplished anything truly.
6) Getting anywhere in the base is simply a pain in the ♥♥♥. You cannot sprint inside the giant labyrinth that is XCOM headquarters, so it takes forever to go from person to person to talk to anyone for missions. Also, there is a decontamination room in between the lab and the rest of the base. While this feature is neat to travel through the first couple of times, after about 30 times you start getting really agitated/impatient, really quick.
7) The storyline is not all that immersive for the player sadly enough. A few moral choices here and there, but in the end it is linear, monotonous, and unfulfilling.
These are just a FEW of the issues I have had with this game. It was not worth the $45 that i paid for it, but I hope some of the other XCOM games I received with the pre-order bundle prove to be more worthwhile. I give this game a rating of "an out of this world letdown". This is mainly for all the hype it received, especially in comparison to its predecessor, and by definitely not meeting any of those expectations. Go play XCOM: Enemy Unknown instead--it has an expansion as well which will be a better investment for your money without a doubt.
Edit: Since some people think I was/am "too harsh" in my review and believe all reviews or critiques must have positive aspects in them, I now need to make the following statement:
If a game has a ridiculously overwhelming amount of negative aspects to it that far outweigh the scarce and miniscule amount of "positive" aspects within it, then they are simply not worth mentioning in a review. I played the entirety of this game to ensure readers that I make a THOROUGH review based on my impressions of the gameplay itself experienced firsthand. Most of the time my reviews tend to be positive even...however, this game was so insanely bad that I could not help but try to sway others to not waste their time like I did. Also considering I was one of the few people to pre-order this game based off of the beautiful game known as XCOM: Enemy Unknown, I needed to make sure I got my $45 worth out of this atrocity, no matter how terrible it truly is and forever shall be. I hope you all enjoyed my review and I thank you for your time reading it and this comment :) Hopefully, you do not make the same mistake I did in purchasing this game at a high price.
TL;DR: The game is incredibly bad. Do not purchase. Ever. Unless on steam sale (75% off or more only applies here). Do not feed them more money for it at full price. Hell, the Steam Store Score (triple alliteration ftw) for this game should give you an alert to how bad it truly is if nothing else...some people like it...but far more do not care for the game in comparison--and for good reason.

Cool little title to try out.  The developer states in a pinned thread that it's basically a demo/student project to showcase what they can do.  Didn't check just how much time they really had, but I definitely liked what was there.  Obviously I couldn't take in everything since it's in Chinese...and I don't know Chinese.  However, there were pop ups that at least told me what buttons SHOULD do something and was easy enough to work it out from there.
As a tech demo of sorts I can see various aspects in place that I never got to make use of
- item drops from downed enemies (currency?)
- some sort of magic bar, though it could be innate to their development system
- various combos using the attack keys on the controller (one button was mentioned but I couldn't seem to do anything with it)
One thing I wish I knew a translation for was the options menu.  There's a window/full screen option that's easy to identify but there's one that I'm not sure what it's for.  At first I thought it was for gamma or some kind of lighting option, but I realized it works as a way to refill your life bar (and that of the boss when you fight him).  Odd...
Overall, it's pretty short.  I realize I spent a hour on this but there would be a lot less if I hadn't spent time taking screenshots of various things (or just messing around regardless). xD  On the plus side, it's probably the EASIEST 100% achievement game ever.  There's only one achievement and you get it when you open the game. :P
I had fun with it and am curious what the developer does next.  Hopefully the next title(s?) could have English support but I understand why this one doesn't for what it is.

All my life I have been empty. The doctors could not tell me why I was so depressed, and I never knew myself until today. I needed to experience my life as a goat. Goat Simulator has filled the void in my life.
I knew as soon as I hit the truck with my goat that this was what I had been missing. I flew through the air in slow motion, tongue flying around, hitting the edge of the map and rebounding back, landing on (and falling through) the roof of a house. I could not get out, but that did not matter. I was treated with the ability to look down into the house beneath me, seeing the unsuspecting people casually sitting at their computers, oblivious to the sheer terror of the goat above them.
Whether it was playing football with a basketball, swinging lampposts into groups of people or even doing 1080 degree flips, there was no limit to life as a goat. I didn't think it could get any better than this.
I was wrong.
As I jumped and screamed my way around the map, leaving a path of destruction in my wake, I happened upon a golden statue. Curiosity overtook me and I resisted the urge to grab it no longer. My life as a goat changed completely. I had a jetpack.
I knew that this was meant to be, and what my mission from the Great Coffee Stain in the sky was. I was granted the supergoat power of being able to lift people and cars with my tongue. I could survive any impact. I could slow down time with mere thought. Now I could fly. It was time for world domination. Humanity had to be silenced so that the new goat overlords could reign supreme.
All the humans are dead or enslaved. I have won. I am the goat, the goat is me.
Go and goat this game. I kid you not, for mere bucks you can experience a sandbox like no other. Destruction, mayhem, death defying stunts. Seriously, there are more than 921 million goats in the world. Killing the humans was just part of the game. This is a SIMULATOR. Do you understand? A SIMULATOR. This can happen. There are enough goats out there to enslave us and/or kill us.
It is your duty as a human to get this game, so that you may truly know your enemy. An enemy people do not take seriously, an enemy that we know nothing about. Coffee Stain studios have granted us the insight into the true terrifying reality of the impending Goatpocalypse. This is your weapon against the goats. Be prepared, for the goats are coming to get us.

'Evolve Stage 2' is a game about surviving against the odds.
The game is basically Hunt and be Hunted, You choose from 1 of 27 playable Characters in 5 different Roles.
There are 2 Main roles in the game, Monster and Hunters, The goal of the 7 playable Monsters is to 'Eat, Evolve and Overpower'
while the goal of the 20 playable Hunters is simply to kill the Monster before it evolves into Stage 3 and destroys the
'Power Relay'located on each of the 4 Maps. A team of Monsters consists of 1 insanely powerful beast controlled by a Player or
in some circumstances an Artificial Intelligence (A.I).
A team of Hunters consists of 1 Character from each of the 4 Hunter Roles -- Assault, Trapper, Medic and Support;
The Assaults job is simply to output damage at an unrivaled rate with a shield that grants temporary Invincibility but at a cost
of a significantly longer Cooldown before it can be used again.
The Trapper is Self-Explanitory, They have a wide array of weaponry that can Trap, Slow and Stun Monsters, Trappers are also
given a Radar that upon activation reveals the general direction of the Monster on the Compass at the bottom of the screen.
The Medic is also Self-Explanitory, Medics main purpose is to be a backline Supportive Character that provides Healing to injured
Hunters, Medics are given an Ability that heals all Hunters in a specific Radius but at a cost of a longer then normal Cooldown.
The Support provides various buffs to a Teammate, Whether it be providing a Temporary Damage Shield to a teammate in need or
an Orbital Bombardment of rockets at a targeted location. Supports are given an Ability that shields ALL Teammates for a small
amount of time.
There are 2 Gamemodes in the game, The regular 'Hunt' Gamemode where the goal is to either destroy the Power Relay or kill
the Monster whereas the second Gamemode, 'Arena' is a Best-Of series of Rounds where the team of Hunters will fight within a large Circular blue
Dome that the Monster and Hunters can not escape, The team that defeats the other will win a round. Normal Arena matches last
for 3 Rounds which, Upon completion the team with the most rounds won will win the Match.
The game also features a rather rewarding Progression System, Upon completing any match you will be awarded with the games Currency,
"Silver Keys" and a chunk of Experience. Experience applies to a Progression System for your overall Player Level and the
Character you played that match, Each level you earn with both Character and Player level
are awarded with a certain amount of Silver Keys and in some circumstances a Customizable Badge, Weapon or even Character Skin.
There are currently 40 Levels per Character (Total of 1,080 Levels) and 50 Levels per Profile.

This is my first time doing a review on steam as I usually can't be bothered but I just had to for GRW. I picked up the game after playing a few rounds of Ghost War during the free weekend and haven't been able to put it down since. My only major issue right now is that the price point of $80 is a bit steep just for the multiplayer portion of the game. If you're planning on utilizing both campaign/coop and ghost war however I think the game definitely has some value to it (again I have not tried the campaign but it definitely looks like there is value there). If the game were to go on sale again in the future and you're a shooter fan definitely without a doubt pick up the game, the multiplayer alone is worth it.

First off: It's not a bad game. It's solid for what it does - mostly being a Cover Shooter.
But it feels lackluster in every regard.
The main discipline, the actual tactical shooting doesn't feel very tactical unless late in the game. The AI is unreliable at best, the options are limited to targeting a specific enemy, moving to a position and a very limited set of active abilities which almost all offer some kind of damage output increase instead of supporting utility. The enemies feel very bullet spongy even on lower difficulties and only pose a challenge through their masses combined with the team-AI running into open field, especially in the second half of the game.
Customizationwise the game doesn't offer much. A handful of weapons in the archetypes of assault rifle, shotgun, sniper rifle, sidearm and heavy arms divided into three ammunition types. Bullets against unarmored, Laser against shields and plasma with a damage over time effect, though the difference doesn't matter much in the field and your basically limited to whatever you find during the missions anyway. The skill trees offer some choices which again don't account for much, just as the backpacks. It all feels like more was planned but eventually cut.
All of this makes the game play like a generic cover shooter for a long time.
The level design offers some pretty nice scenary and fantastic atmosphere at times but with large gaps filled with generic corridors and obstacles (and some invisible walls) conviniently placed to only allow a narrow path. Whenever you see a wider area, be assured to have enemies incoming. Since the linear design doesn't allow much exploration, it is surprising that the paths branching left and right of the main path are often pointless and empty or give a new backpack schematic at best - which you can mostly also get from the dispatch side missions.
The story is based on the older (50s - 60s) SciFi movies with slight horror mixed in between. Think of 'Invasion of the Body Snatchers' or similar - or Captain Scarlet and the Mysterons which has basically the same premise ;)
Again it feels cut on every end. There are some illogical jumps in character behaviour, descissions which don't matter at all, dialogue which repeats itself or is even nonsensical and the campaign feels very rushed with various Dei ex machina. The writing also does a very good job of making the main character as unlikeable as humanly possibile, throwing out oneliners like Duke Nukem which drip from pathos and stupidity.
The whole XCOM feeling from the classic games or the remake is barely there apart from the alien names - you're only fighting on US American soil, with US Americans and have no contact to or intel about any other nation. Even the mission map is limited to mainland USA, making the whole global invasion a very US-centric thing.
There are also some very annonying design decissions in the game:
Firstly it's Checkpoints only. Died in the 3rd wave of a shootout? Feel lucky if it places you right at the beginning of the fight instead of some rooms prior. It doesn't even allow free saving outside the missions during exploring the base.
Placement of team members or deployable abilities makes you basically move them along the physical path in the same 3rd person view instead of ignoring obstacles, stairs or maybe giving you more of a bird's eye view. All while the battle doesn't pause but only slows down, which means moving a mortally wounded squad mate out of the danger zone may end up with him being shot during the command giving.
Having sprint on the same button as taking cover leads to some strange positioning sometimes, especially since you can't stear during sprinting.
During the first part of the game you will open doors, having a short scene of your character securing the room with raised weapon through which he is uncontrollable and which is always pointless since there are never enemies behing those doors. Nor anything other to speak of. Later in the game this suddenly stops but is replaced with long empty corridors and elevator rides during which nothing happens.
Boring storyline and stupid AI

A great game for those who love the dating sim genre and a good game for those who don't.
Hatoful Boyfriend is a parody dating sim where instead of romancing other people, you romance birds. The routes for each of the birds are fairly short compared to other dating sims out there but they are all funny and enjoyable (and some downright bizarre). However, if you're looking for a lot of romance, then I wouldn't say this game is for you. While there is romance in some routes, it is mainly left to the readers imagination after the route is finished. I would say though, that if you are a fan of dating sims and otome games, you will probably get more out of the game as it parodies stereotype characters found in a lot of typical dating sims.
Even if you aren't a huge fan of dating sims, I would recommend the game alone for the alternative story which contrasts greatly to the main game (and is a lot longer than the average route). The alternative story answers all the mysteries hinted at in the main game and gives a explanation to why you are the only human in a school for birds. Let me just say, if you're a fan of mysteries and thrillers you will probably like this part.
I actually bought the deluxe edition, which features: the soundtrack (36 tracks), the original game (in english), a ten page manga with 4koma strips and some illustrations (in both Japanese and English), two Okosan wallpapers and a 35 page yearbook, featuring pictures of the backgrounds and characters. While the extra stuff is great, I don't think I would pay full price for the deluxe pack. However, if you are a big fan of the series and the original game it might be worth it.

Not bad
Story
You are a kid that goes Trick and Treating with their sibling who is swiftly kidnapped by monsters. Now it is your job to go door to door trick or treating, complete quests, and fight monsters. It’s pretty much a standard RPG with a halloween theme painted on it. The story isn’t bad and it follows Double Fine’s formula well (kid looking game with often adult adventures that is eccentric). There are some dark elements to the game which come out really well and the whole game has a theme of child wonder to it. You fight as real transformers, unicorns, and vampires while facing daemons. It sounds like a kid fantasy. However, the story isn’t flushed out as Psychonauts for example and I don't really remember much
Gameplay
It’s a standard RPG (with a twist). The main point is to go around to all of the stores/houses and trick or treat. Different areas are blocked out until you can unlock certain areas. This is mostly done through monster fights. Overall, this system is nice as it moves the plot along via your actions but gets very repetitive near the end as you just end up going from monster fight to monster fight.
Speaking of which, the monster battles are a bit simple. You can have up to 3 characters each of which has a regular move and a special ability with a long cool down. Additionally, you have different patches you can apply which are absolutely necessary to stand a chance. It took me a while to find a pair that worked for me but in the end, it was all just the same thing over and over until the end. Overall, I found the system a bit simple and I don’t play RPGs much
Performance:
With a 4790k, GTX 970, and 16GB of ram, it ran at either 30 or 60fps for me. It didn’t vary in between those two numbers but rather certain scenes and areas were stuck at 30. The game isn’t aiming to be realistic so the graphics are cartoony.
Overall, the game was OK. I’m reminded of South Park: The Stick of Truth a lot and honestly, I would recommend playing that over this game. It’s not bad but just kinda meh to above meh.

Alright, lets get this over with.
First of all, I love this game, I think that it can bring lots of fun and a ton of hours of FPS gameplay. Its moddability is awsome and is what drives me to this game. I like and play this game like I would any other FPS and just unleash hell onto any poor raiders in my sights. Mindlessly tearing apart enemys like tissue paper.
But as a storybased RPG, it fails completely.
The "RPG" part of the game is a joke in my opinion. A shell of its former self when compared to previous fallout titles.
The first big mistake Bethesda made when creating the game is to give a voice to your "created character", ripping away of any chance to make your character unique, you are forced with an avenge your family story that is boring and downright not worth it. Another big problem with the game is the horrible dialouge options, almost (if not all) of the options you are given is 1. Sarcastic 2. Persuasion 3. positive remark 4. negative remark. In older games, you can choose exactly what you want to say and even have your perks and skills matter in some dialouge options and could completly change the side-story (and sometimes the main-quests) completly.
Then they ruin the perk and skill system, when in previous games where you can actually suck in one area (like using energy weapons) and be the master of something else (like using explosives). Now your "perk" system is filled with slight tweaks to make you slightly better in one very specific aspect that will only come in handy in one or two situations in the entire game. You cannot suck in one aspect or another, you can use any weapon without fail, you can mod any weapon no matter how much you use it or neglect it. Dumb.
Another failed part is the settlement system. Don't get me wrong the feeling of building what is the equivalent of a small town or fort to call your own is amazing in of itself, its when it has absolutly no effect on the wasteland or characters itself is the problem here. There is no reason to build settlements, absolutly none, their is no downsides to creating settlements just as their is no positive benefits. Unless you want to create your own town/house/fort to dump all of your stuff in there is no true benefit that is worthwhile.
And, the worst of all, the quests. While in previous fallout games where side quests and things you say actually matter, and can have unchangable events happen, here it is completly stripped away and remade into this "go here, kill enemies, get paid" system. There is no wrong answers or choices in this game, its all super happy funtime land where you have no choice but to obey the braindead sidequests for absolutly no reason but to shoot things.
The only reason I play this game as much as I do is the fact that modding can help the game soooo much. But the fact that I had to download sooooo many mods (and I mean a LOT) in order to get this game feeling close to a proper fallout game is a negative in itself. It goes to show how much Bethesda is willing to assume that the Modding community will fix the game shows how lax and lazy Bethesda is getting with their RPG games as of late.
I rate this game a 6/10 if you play it as a brainless shooter with light RPG elements. But as a fallout game, with all of the "perks" and the sorry excuse of side quests, I rate this game as a 3/10. It could have been the best fallout title to date if only Bethesda realized that the people who play the fallout games are not a bunch of 8 year olds that need their hands held through every moment.
If you want a good Fallout game, buy Fallout: New Vegas, or Fallout 1 and 2. If you want to be treated like a little kid and have copy and paste side quests and have your hand held through every situation with no possiblity of bad things happening, buy Fallout 4.
Do you know what we need? Obsidian to create a new fallout game with the RPG aspects, DLC, and stories of Fallout New Vegas with the gunplay and crafting system of Fallout 4. THAT would be lightyears ahead of this failed attempt of a game.

Ευχάριστο, ευφάνταστο, αυθεντικό και πολύ τίμιο όσον αφορά στη χρηματοδότηση που αξίωσε. Αυτή η πρόταση θεωρώ ότι περιγράφει όσο καλύτερα γίνεται το “A Fowl Fleet”, ένα σύντομης διάρκειας adventure game που διαθέτει έναν γεμάτο και ζωντανό κόσμο, συνοδεία εξαιρετικών voice overs και πολύ αρμονικής μουσικής ενορχήστρωσης.
A pleasant, imaginative, original and fair –regarding the amount of money it targeted on Kickstarter- adventure game. It doesn’t last long, but features a rich and vivid world, accompanied by excellent voice overs and harmonious music orchestration.

Nelly Cootalot so thoroughly embraces its retro inspirations, that an uncharitable person might call it out-dated. However, it breezes along with such warm-hearted charm, boundless likability, and its none-more-British sense of humour that it's hard to criticise. It's populated with a cast of great characters, with the eponymous Nelly as the pirate heroine out to save all bird-kind from the schemes of her nemesis, Baron Widebeard. The puzzles are fair, logical, and satisfying to solve; you'll rarely spend time trying random inventory items with everything in sight and are unlikely to be forced to consult a walkthrough. Don't forget to consult your fowl companion, Sebastian, for some of the games funniest lines and hints if you lose track of what you're doing.
This game is an easy recommendation for fans of pirate adventures of yesteryear (you know the ones...) and point-and-click games in general. You'll spend your entire playthrough with a big smile on your face or your money back (maybe).

I don't care about reviews much and you shouldn't, this game is not a RTS or well not what a true X-COM game is BUT, that doesn't mean you should pass on it. The review scores have been unfair to this gem, its worth having for a few reasons,
its a hybrid RTS so that will turn people off a bit, its a shooter, with stats like fallout and you give orders to squadmates to use abilities and skills like you do in mass effect, they still can fight on their own but its all about tactics.
the game takes place in retro 50s land, a great change from the futureish style seen today, classic weapons, with aliens lasers make up your equip, and backpacks are kinda like your magic, the more backpacks you find the better skills you can get, one back may give you better armor attack, others may help you take damage.
story is pretty good, i wish it was more in detail but still good enough, you have a base that changes as you progress threw the game, areas change as they are used, you can read files, listen to audio records etc.
if you want to know the game is kinda like mass effect, spec ops the line,ressistance, a bit of killzone, and rainbow six all at once, its not a "easy" game, your not meant to take tone of damage, and on the higher settings it can get extreme if you don't know what you are doing, but once you do its natural. I do rec you play with a controller eg exbox, or emu pad, because it makes giving orders etc alot easier.
the missions are LONG, its been a while since i said that, a few of the missions have been 1hr to 2hrs long and that may throw off some people that want to sit and finish a game fast...but nothing is stopping them from saving and picking it up later, the world has interactive dialog, you may see a ? on the ground next to a body and get detail about it or comments.
I say buy the game, i don't understand why it got a lower score other then sheep reviews or lame shallow people wanting a game they can beat and discard......but its  a rough gem, and if you overlook it's faults, and give it a chance it will grow on it, 4/5

Eu discordo dos meus colegas, acho que XCOM Declassified vale a pena sim, mas apenas se for pego abaixo de R$20. Sim, é um jogo genérico, derivativo etc, mas possui gameplay sólido, uma estória legalzinha, além de ser bonito.
Gameplay: O game é essencialmente um clone de Mass Effect 2. Desde a maneira como o personagem se move até o sistema de combate em sí. E por isso mesmo que o gameplay é sólido. Podem reclamar de outras áreas do jogo quem quiser, e com razão, mas não nisso. Existem em torno de 15 armas e elas se comportam bem diferente em combate. Além disso, o jogo conta com avanço de nível, uma árvore de talentos, 4 classes de agentes (além da classe única do PC) e outros aspectos que lembram um RPG de estratégia...novamente eu reforço, esse game é essencialmente um clone de Mass Effect 2. Até mesmo entre as missões você pode andar pela base XCOM e conversar com NPCs, fazer pequenas missões escolhidas num mapa, na ordem que você quiser, igualzinho você faz na Normandy.
Inteligência Artificial: No caso dos seus companheiros de batalha deixa a desejar, mas no caso dos inimigos não. Seus companheiros frequentemente ignoram algumas ordens suas, se colocam em posição de perigo desnecessariamente ou saem de locais que você previamente designou. Mas de maneira alguma isso quebra o jogo, ou acontece sem parar. Apenas naquelas batalhas mais longas com inimigos mais fortes é preciso ter mais cuidado com eles e checar o que eles estão fazendo com mais frequência. Zerei o game no Hard e sem perder nenhum agente em campo. Os inimigos são decentes, fogem de granadas suas, tentam te flanquear, se reposicionam se você está flanqueado eles etc.
Gráficos e Cenários: Esqueça utilizar DX11 nesse jogo, dá uns erros, pequenos lags etc, e jogando com DX10 você só perde Tesselation. Dito isso, o jogo é bem bonito. Nem precisa ter uma placa de vídeo super para rodar tudo no High/Ultra, sem pop ins, glitches em texturas etc. A ambientação do jogo também é muito boa e faz um trabalho excelente em transmitir o clima da década de 60, nesse sentido lembra muito seriados como Mad Men ou jogos como LA Noire. Os cenários são bem variados e diferentes, apesar de alguns serem um pouco "vazios", faltando um pouco mais de detalhes, itens etc.
Animação: É uma faca de dois lados. A animação facial é bem acima da média, a animação corporal bem abaixo. Os rostos são bem feitos, se articulam bem e conferem com clareza o estado de espírito dos personagens - exceto da agente Weaver...tem alguma coisa ali que eu não gosto muito e não consigo achar o que é - mas a animação do corpo é extremamente limitada, elas são bem feitas, mas são muito poucas. Nem tanto dos NPCs, mas o personagem principal - William Carter - possui exatamente duas posturas quando fala com alguém: ou está de braços cruzados e uma das mão no queixo ou ele dá dois pequenos tapinhas com uma mão aberta, enquanto cerra o punho da que está recebendo os tapinhas.
História e Diálogos: Ela começa bem, tem uma boa premissa mas acaba não entregando toda a sua promessa. As vezes eu tenho a impressão de que o jogo inicialmente seria bem maior. No início os fatos são melhor explicados, contados, mas perto do fim a história dá umas reviravoltas meio sem sentido, as ações de alguns personagens não são muito bem explicadas, coisas assim. O diálogo como um todo é okay, mas o do personagem principal é SUPER cafona...pense num filme mega patriota americano de guerra fria e você vai ter uma boa ideia do que esperar. Na realidade todos os demais NPCs são melhores e mais interessantes que o tal do William Carter.
Quem deve comprar esse jogo: Mesmo não sendo uma fiel entrada ao universo XCOM, The Bureau ainda consegue transmitir bem aquele clima da série. Se você sempre quis jogar Mass Effect mas com toda a mitologia e clima de um jogo XCOM...Que bom! Por que agora você pode! Eu recomendaria o jogo apenas se for comprado abaixo de R$20, se você curte Mass Effect, XCOM, e está atrás de um RPG mais curtinho, que você bate em 15-20h. É um típico jogo B, possui bons sistemas, não é quebrado, tem gameplay bom e estória okay.
Nota: 6,5!

I'm a fan of the XCom franchise, but I went into this one very skeptical due to its more action oriented design than the traditional titles. Once I started play tho I was pleasantly surprised. The game is obviously very visually amazing but they didn't waste all their time on that and leave you with a shallow piece of crap.
The plot is very well written and engaging and better thought out, imo, than the one used for XCOM Enemy Unknown. While there is no grand strategy element to this, the way you handle your 3 man teams has an excellent amount of tactical play to it. The time dilation used keeps the game going but allows you a certain level of precision for giving orders and using special abilities.
Despite the fact that the overall plot will remain the same, there are numerous choices within the game that will affect how events play out. This gives the game a surprising amount of replay value. I also recommend the Hangar 6 DLC which gives even more life to the game and fleshes out the story even more.

Bleh - I couldn't be bothered to finish this. It had a lot of potential, but it just isn't much fun.
- Team AI is horrid. I can live with them being mostly pointless or just serving as special ability vehicles, ala Mass Effect. However they are aggressively stupid. Periodically they will decide their cover is bad, and charge forward into the enemy, or way over-extend themselves. This would be a stupid nuisance, if it wasn't for the permadeath. If you could tell them "go here" and rely on them STAYING there, that would be ok too.. but the moment an enemy lobs a grenade, they take off.
- Abilities are lackluster. Only 3-4 abilities per class is sort of boring. Often a guy would level and I would bring up their level-up menu to see what neat stuff they would get, and be disapointed.
- Enemies are bullet sponges.
- Most weapons don't feel very effective.
- While the game starts by sort of implying there will be upgrades and upgrade trees, it is boring. There are laser upgrades to the main weapons (that are not even reliably an upgrade.. I'm convinced the Laser SMB is worse then all the bullet weapons). Every character gets basically 1 gun, and 1 backpack. The backpacks each have a different type of buff (+dmg to shielded enemies, +dmg to headshots, etc), and thats it for their equipment.
All told, I was fairly disapointed in this. I figured at 7 bucks or so (the sale price I paid) it would be a good time with action similar to mass effect but meh. If they kept the combat system but had more depth to the powers, more depth to leveling, better AI, and more depth to equipment, this could have been awesome.

Treat this as the squad based cover based shooter it is, and it's quite enjoyable. It's not AAA quality in all aspects of production - Scenery is reused (Obviously the alien structures) over and over again and it doesn't ever quite feel epic, but the story is solid and there is at least the illusion of choice every so often. It does have a fairly good plot and I put at least 15 hours in to finish it. There's very little offline management required but you can wander around the base, even if it is knowingly unnecessary if you just want to get through the game.

This game tries to straddle the fence between being a first person shooter, and a turn based strategy.  I feel that it didn't accomplish either of these tasks well.  While the game isn't horrible I believe it doesn't live up to the XCOM name.  If you're looking for you alien killing fix I would extremely highly recommend XCOM: Enemy Unknown
